title: FireGuard: A Generalized Microarchitecture for Fine-Grained Security Analysis on OoO Superscalar Cores
problem: Generic programmable support for fine-grained instruction-level security analysis on real out-of-order (OoO) superscalar processors; existing abstract simulators cannot capture critical path and contention issues in real microarchitectures.
motivation: Security guarantees in high-performance processors require hardware support for fine-grained instruction analysis; real OoO superscalar implementation is challenging due to complex instruction pipelines and resource contention.
method: FireGuard is a microarchitecture enabling instruction-level security analysis on real out-of-order superscalar processors—modern chips that run multiple instructions simultaneously. It combines hardware design, system-on-chip integration, new processor instructions, and a programming model that lets developers instrument security checks without slowing the processor's critical path (longest chain of dependent operations) or causing contention (waits for shared resources). The design was validated on Apple M1-Pro, Huawei Kirin-960, and Intel i7-12700F.
key_novelty: FireGuard is the first programmable system for analyzing individual instructions' security on real out-of-order superscalar processors with minimal silicon overhead.
contributions: First fine-grained instruction analysis implementation on real OoO superscalar cores
Complete end-to-end system: microarchitecture, SoC integration, ISA, programming model
Parallel scalability with simultaneous security and performance guarantees
Less than 1% silicon area overhead on modern SoCs (M1-Pro, Kirin-960, i7-12700F)

metrics.other: Parallel scalability with security and performance maintained

primary_theme: Fine-grained instruction analysis microarchitecture for OoO superscalar security
